reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports the premise that ML (SVM) can predict yield strength with ~11% error at 20°C, but it does not provide evidence for the other key premises: multi-fidelity frameworks, hierarchical descriptors for fracture, prediction of modulus/toughness, or the claimed 10x computational speedup. The hypothesis relies heavily on unsupported extrapolations from a single yield-strength study.
premises: ML can predict yield strength of HEAs with ~11-13.5% error at 20-600°C
A multi-fidelity ML framework can reduce computational cost by ~10x vs. traditional methods
Hierarchical microstructural descriptors can mediate local stress distributions and fracture behavior
The framework can predict Young's modulus and fracture toughness, not just yield strength
The method will fail if microstructural heterogeneity diverges from the training dataset
